info.title: Magna Carta API
info.description: The Magna Carta legal practice-management API. Every operation is enforced at one chokepoint (tenancy → authn → RBAC → idempotency → rate-limit); errors are RFC 9457 problem documents.

state.description: What this person still has to do: choose how they join a firm, or wait while the firm they asked for is built.

fileStorage.description: Its file storage has been allocated.

encryptionKey.description: Its encryption key has been minted.

activated.description: The firm is active and its owner is recorded — the last step.

stalled.description: The build stopped and is no longer being retried. Reported because it is the one state on a waiting screen that will not clear by waiting.

FirmBuildProgress.description: Present only while a firm is being built; how far it has got.

state.description: Whether this account's member record has reached the firm's own database. `provisioning` is a wait, not a permission somebody has to grant; `stalled` is that write having been given up on, which waiting will not fix; `unknown` is a read that did not answer, which is not a verdict about the account.

status.description: A deactivated member is still listed: they remain the responsible attorney on matters they carried and the author of what they filed, and dropping the row would print those cells as an unfilled gap rather than as the person who is no longer here. Nothing sets this yet; no route deactivates a member.

roleNames.description: The names of the roles this member holds; empty where they hold none.

hasProfessionalProfile.description: Whether a professional profile has been written for this member — the title, admissions and signature block a pleading states. False means unwritten, never unreadable.

roleName.description: The role the invitation names, or null where it names none.

A role of this firm, by name, for the invited member to hold on arrival. A name that is not one of the firm's roles is refused rather than dropped — an invitation quietly landing without the role somebody chose is worse than one that does not land.

parentRoleId.description: The role this one is a sub-role of, or null for a top-level role. A sub-role adds to its parent and is only ever held together with it, so its permissions are the ones it adds.

permissions.description: The permission keys this role carries, in registry form. Empty where the role carries none, which is a real state rather than a missing answer.

memberCount.description: How many ACTIVE members hold this role — who a change to it would reach.

roleIds.description: The roles this member is to hold, as a whole set rather than a change to it. The server diffs against what they hold now, so a role in both lists is never momentarily removed. An empty array leaves the member holding nothing.

prefix.description: What goes before the name, as the whole line: several honorifics is ordinary, and the line as written is what is printed. Free text — the suggestions a screen offers constrain nothing.

suffix.description: What follows the name, as the whole line — "III, Esq." is one person's suffix.

displayName.description: The line the parts read as, and what the platform prints. Rendered from the parts where the person has stated any; otherwise the name their account was created with.

partsStated.description: Whether the person has ever stated their parts. False means the display name is the one line their account was created with, and a screen may offer a reading of it for them to confirm — never store one on their behalf.

suffix.description: What follows the name, as the whole line — "III, Esq." is one person's suffix.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the bytes, which keys the object.

role.description: What is being registered. `account` — the default, and the only value the joining surface sends — registers a PERSON: confirming it creates their account, and which firm they belong to is settled afterwards, signed in. The other three are the superseded role fork, kept so a registration started before the reflow still completes: `clientOfFirm` and `firmMember` are joined by invitation, and `foundFirm` builds a firm at confirmation.

password.description: The password the person is choosing, 8-128 characters. Required for the doors that create an account (`account`, `foundFirm`); ignored by the two invitation doors, which create nothing.

kind.description: What the invitee becomes: a member of the firm, or a client of it with portal access only.
What the invitee becomes: a member of the firm, or a client of it with portal access only.

admissions.description: Bar admissions as running prose the firm writes — never parsed, never guessed.

signatureBlock.description: The multi-line block a pleading signs off with, stored with its line breaks. It becomes a merge field once the assembly engine emits real line breaks; until then it is recorded here so nothing has to be retyped when that lands.

displayName.description: What the firm is called to its clients — on invoices, in the portal, and on every generated document. Never the provisioning handle behind it.
The firm's human-facing name. Required and non-empty: a firm with no name prints none on the documents it sends.

incrementMinutes.description: The firm's minimum billing increment: what a captured duration rounds TO, in minutes. Six — a tenth of an hour — is the prevailing default. It is also what one BILLING UNIT is worth, so a firm on quarter hours and a firm on tenths mean different amounts of work by the same number of units.

roundingDirection.description: How the firm resolves a duration that falls between increments.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the file's bytes, lowercase hex.

kind.description: What kind of document this template is. wordProcessing is a Word document with {{field}} placeholders typed into it — the default, and what most templates are. pdfForm is a fillable PDF your firm already has, such as a court form: its boxes are filled in by this system once you confirm which merge field each one is filled from. Defaults to wordProcessing.

What kind of document this template is. wordProcessing is a Word document with {{field}} placeholders typed into it — the default, and what most templates are. pdfForm is a fillable PDF your firm already has, such as a court form: its boxes are filled in by this system once you confirm which merge field each one is filled from. Defaults to wordProcessing.

convertMergeFields.description: Whether to convert Word merge fields in the uploaded document into this system's {{field}} form. Leave this off and the document registers exactly as you authored it, with every Word merge field listed in the response and recorded against the template — but those fields are not filled in by this system, so every document assembled from the template prints the text Word last cached in them, and each assembly reports that too. Turning it on rewrites each one in place: the document registered is then not the document uploaded.

stripMacros.description: Whether to remove macro content from the uploaded document. A template is run against privileged client data, so one carrying macros cannot be stored: without this, an upload that contains any is refused, and the response lists what was found. Turning it on removes the macro project along with the content-type and relationship declarations that reference it, re-checks the result from scratch, and refuses the registration outright if anything survived — the document registered is then not the document uploaded. Uploading a macro-free copy of the file is the other way through.

fieldMappings.description: For a fillable-PDF template: which merge field each box on the form is filled from, by the form's own field name. Nothing is guessed — a box you do not name here is left empty in every document assembled from the template, and the response lists every one of them along with the boxes whose names happen to match a merge field exactly, which you can confirm rather than choose. Each entry is remembered for this firm, so a second form using the same field names arrives already filled in. Ignored for a Word template, whose binding is the {{field}} an author typed.

clientEntityId.description: The directory entity the firm acts for. Given, the client's party link is written in the same batch as the matter, so billing, trust and the conflicts check find the client from the day the matter exists. The display name still travels beside it as the denormalized caption.

fileRetentionMinimumYears.description: The firm's minimum retention for a closed matter's paper file, in whole years after the close. 0 means the firm states no minimum; the platform never picks a period.

physicalFileLocationId.description: The office where the firm keeps this matter's own paper file. Not the office the matter is run out of (locationId): a folder travels, and a matter opened at one office can be boxed at another or at a remote store the firm keeps as an office. Null clears it, which is the honest answer where nobody knows where the file is.

fileDestroyOn.description: The date (YYYY-MM-DD) the matter's paper file may be destroyed after, stated by the person closing it — no earlier than the firm's minimum retention after the close (GET /api/v1/matters/settings) — or null for none. Absent records nothing. A reminder only: nothing is deleted when the date arrives.

assignmentRole.description: The working role — originating attorney, supervising attorney, billing attorney, assigned paralegal, or the firm's own wording of one. Matched by its letters and digits, so spelling and separators are free. The responsible attorney is refused here: that fact lives on the matter itself.

validFrom.description: The first day the assignment holds, as a civil date (YYYY-MM-DD), inclusive. Omit for an assignment that starts open-ended.

validTo.description: The last day the assignment holds, as a civil date (YYYY-MM-DD), inclusive — an assignment through 2026-08-07 still staffs the matter for the whole of that day. Omit for a current assignment; ending one later stamps the exact ending moment instead.

courtEntityId.description: The court, as a Directory organisation — its name and identity live there.

judgeEntityId.description: The assigned judge, as a Directory person.

clientDesignation.description: What this court's caption calls the client's side — Plaintiff, Petitioner.

opposingDesignation.description: What this court's caption calls the other side — Defendant, Respondent.

courtEntityId.description: The court, as a Directory organisation — its name and identity live there.

judgeEntityId.description: The assigned judge, as a Directory person.

opposingDesignation.description: What this court's caption calls the other side — Defendant, Respondent.

courtEntityId.description: The court, as a Directory organisation — its name and identity live there.

judgeEntityId.description: The assigned judge, as a Directory person.

clientDesignation.description: What this court's caption calls the client's side — Plaintiff, Petitioner.

opposingDesignation.description: What this court's caption calls the other side — Defendant, Respondent.

destroyOn.description: The civil date (YYYY-MM-DD) on or after which the firm may destroy its own paper file for this matter. The firm states it; the platform derives no date and deletes nothing when it arrives — it is a reminder on the matter and on the firm calendar. Null clears it.

decedentEntityId.description: The decedent, as a Directory person — every name rendering reads from there.

estateEntityId.description: The estate's own Directory organisation, where the firm keeps one — the home of the estate's encrypted tax identifier.

estateStyle.description: The estate's style exactly as the court has it — stored, never composed.

decedentEntityId.description: The decedent, as a Directory person — every name rendering reads from there.

estateEntityId.description: The estate's own Directory organisation, where the firm keeps one — the home of the estate's encrypted tax identifier.

estateStyle.description: The estate's style exactly as the court has it — stored, never composed.

decedentEntityId.description: The decedent, as a Directory person — every name rendering reads from there.

estateEntityId.description: The estate's own Directory organisation, where the firm keeps one — the home of the estate's encrypted tax identifier.

estateStyle.description: The estate's style exactly as the court has it — stored, never composed.

possessivePronoun.description: As in: the signature is hers.

verbNumber.description: Which verb form the set takes: "singular" for she is / he is, "plural" for they are. Recorded rather than worked out — nothing about the forms themselves says which.

DirectoryPronounSet.description: The complete set of pronouns a person stated, or null where they stated none — which is the ordinary case and not a gap to fill in. Recorded whole: a partly supplied set is refused, because a document rendering one set's pronoun in one clause and another's in the next is wrong in a way nobody catches by reading it.

permitted.description: May the firm use this contact point. Defaults to true. A contact point the person asked the firm not to use is recorded with the permission withdrawn and a note saying so, never deleted: deleting it loses the instruction along with the value.

preferred.description: Is this the one route the person asked to be reached by. At most one per entity across email, phone and address together, because that preference is a single answer about every channel; promoting one demotes whichever was preferred before, in any of the three.

note.description: Why the contact point may not be used, or how it should be.

status.description: What the firm found when it last tried to confirm this contact point. A failed status records returned mail, a bounced message or a disconnected line. It never blocks a send: it is surfaced to whoever is about to send, and the send proceeds.

detail.description: What the failure said, in the words it said it.

number.description: The number as it was written. Stored verbatim and never rewritten; the structured columns beside it go null when it cannot be split, so an unparseable number is still recorded.

label.description: The plaintext part a list shows without a reveal: the state or country that issued a licence, the jurisdiction behind a bar number, who an account is held with. Required where the type has one; never any part of the value.

secret.description: An account's secret, sealed beside its number and never indexed.

personIs.description: Which end of the edge the person is. The type says which way a membership reads (employment runs person to organization); the screen decides and the record keeps it.

nameRole.description: What this name is to the entity: its current name, a former one, a maiden name, a trading name. An open catalog, not a closed enum.

isCurrent.description: True for the one name the entity answers to today.

displayName.description: The name as it was recorded. Null for an organization: an organization's name row keeps only the case-folded form, so a caller falls back to normalizedDisplay and shows an honest lowercase former name rather than an invented capitalization.

normalizedDisplay.description: The case-folded, punctuation-stripped form the search and conflicts corpus matches on. Always present, for every name row of either kind.

validTo.description: When the name stopped being used, or null while it still is.

recordedAt.description: When the firm wrote the row down — which is not when the name came into use. A maiden name recorded onto a twenty-year-old file was recorded today and valid decades ago.

total.description: How many records the firm holds under these filters — every page of the walk when the directory is being listed, and the number of records answering when it is being searched, because a ranked answer's size is the answer's and not the book's.

capped.description: True only where a ranked answer (`search`) was cut short: the firm holds more matches than were returned, so narrowing the query reaches the rest. False on every page of the plain index, which is walkable to its end by cursor and never cut.

displayName.description: What to call the record, or null where the directory holds no name for it at all. A caller shows the gap rather than printing the handle.

legalName.description: An organization's legal name where it differs from what the firm calls it; null for a person, and null where the two are the same word.

givenName.description: A person's first name. Null for an organization.

middleName.description: A person's middle name, where the firm recorded one.

familyName.description: A person's last name. Null for an organization, and null for a person who has one name — a record with no family name is one the firm keeps, not one it refuses.

emailAddress.description: The record's default email address — the primary row where one is marked, else the oldest. Null where the firm holds none. Not a contact register: the record's own contact-points read is where every channel lives.

phoneNumber.description: The record's default number, exactly as it was entered and never rewritten.

city.description: The locality of the record's default address.

region.description: The administrative area of the default address — state, province, prefecture — where the country has one.

country.description: The default address's country, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2.

recordedAt.description: When the firm wrote the record down.

changedAt.description: When the record itself last changed. A change to something hanging off it — a name appended, an address added — does not move this.

displayName.description: What to call this entity, or null where the directory holds no name for it at all. A caller renders the gap and never falls back to printing the handle.

mergedIntoId.description: The surviving record this one was folded into, or null while it stands on its own. A list row naming a folded record has to say so.

direction.description: Whether the entity asked about is the FROM end of this edge (outbound) or the TO end (inbound). The relationship reads in the opposite sense from each end.

farEntityId.description: The entity at the other end of the edge.

farDisplayName.description: What to call the far end, resolved through the same naming read the bulk endpoint performs — one lookup for the whole page, never one per row.

matterTitle.description: Null when the link points at a matter the firm no longer holds.

matterNumber.description: Null while the matter is still consultation and undrawn.

archived.description: True for a label the firm has retired. Retired labels are still returned: an entity carrying one must still be able to show what it says.

label.description: The plaintext part: the issuing region, the jurisdiction, who an account is held with.

value.description: The decrypted value — for an account, its number; the username and secret ride beside it.

matchedName.description: WHICH of the entity's names the query landed on. A search that reported only the current name made a hit on a maiden name indistinguishable from a hit on the name typed, which defeats the point of keeping every name an entity has held.

matchedNameRole.description: What that matched name is to the entity — current, former, maiden, dba.

entityKind.description: Which side of the directory the candidate resolves to. 'unknown' means the blocking channels surfaced an entity the node tables no longer hold — a fact worth showing.

displayName.description: What to call the candidate, or null where the directory holds no name for it. A caller shows the gap rather than printing the handle.

capacity.description: The capacity the entity acts in on this matter — Administrator, Trustee, Attorney-in-fact. Recorded by the firm, never inferred; documents that name a capacity read this value and show an honest gap where none was recorded.
The capacity recorded on this link, or null where the firm recorded none. A null is an honest absence and never a default — nothing infers a capacity from the role.

entityKind.description: Which side of the directory the entity resolves to. 'unknown' means the link points at an entity that is no longer there, which is a fact worth showing rather than hiding.

displayName.description: What to call this party, or null when the directory holds no name for the entity. A caller shows the identifier itself rather than inventing a placeholder.

isPrimary.description: This channel's default row — where a message goes when no address was named.

number.description: The number exactly as it was entered. Never rewritten; this is what a screen shows.

contactSystem.description: What technology answers the number. A fax line is a fax by its system, not by a word in a label, so a delivery path can ask the question and get an answer.

countryCallingCode.description: Null where the number carried no country — a national-form number says nothing about which country it belongs to, and the record says so rather than inventing one.

addressType.description: Whether the place physically exists. Personal service turns on this: a post office box is postal and cannot be served, a registered office is physical and can.

dateOfBirth.description: A plain calendar date. Held in the clear because every question a firm asks of a date of birth is a range — is this client a minor, has a limitation period tolled — and a range query over ciphertext is not a query.

deceased.description: Separate from the date, because known dead with the date unknown is a state probate work meets constantly. A recorded date of death implies this flag.

AddressSuggestionsResponse.description: `suggestions` may be empty, which means the country is covered and nothing matched. `no-coverage` means the service holds no addresses for that country, which is not the same thing and must not be shown as though it were. `unavailable` means no address service is provisioned: a person types the address themselves, exactly as before.

suggestionId.description: Opaque. Meaningful only to the resolution operation, short-lived, and able to carry an address — so it is sent back in a request body, never a URL.

label.description: The whole offer on one line, for a list.

kind.description: A group is a building whose units share one street line. It is not an address a record can hold: resolving it answers the addresses inside it.

count.description: For a group, how many addresses it holds.

AddressLookupParts.description: An address as the parts a record stores, named for their position in an address rather than for what any one country calls them.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2: the country the address is in.

query.description: What has been typed so far.

near.description: The region the address is probably in — the subdivision part of an ISO 3166-2 code, without the country (`NC`, not `US-NC`). Ranks nearby addresses first and never hides the rest. Absent, the caller's primary office stands in for it.

AddressResolutionResponse.description: `address` is the parts a record stores. `group` is the addresses inside a group, offered in turn. `expired` is an offer the service no longer knows — nothing went wrong, and the caller asks again.

AddressLocation.description: Where the address is, as the open address data records it. For a map or a distance; not a postal fact.

available.description: Whether this deployment can connect an account at the provider. False means nobody has registered the deployment with the provider, and a screen offers no connection.

accountLabel.description: The account as the provider names it: the member's own sign-in address there.

authorizationUrl.description: The provider's own sign-in page. The browser is sent to it as a whole page.

accountLabel.description: The account as the provider names it: the member's own sign-in address there.

account.description: The member's connected account, or null when they have connected none.

calendars.description: The account's calendars as the provider lists them now. Null when there is no account or the provider could not be asked, in which case rules can be read and not changed.

shownCalendars.description: The account's calendars the member chose to be shown their own events from. Empty until they choose one.

subject.description: An event type's id, or `deadline` for deadlines as one kind.

name.description: The event type's name. Null for the deadline kind.

mayLeave.description: Whether the firm lets this subject be synced at all.

detail.description: How much of an event the firm lets leave: `full`, or `minimal` for the matter number and the event type and nothing else.

subject.description: An event type's id, or `deadline` for deadlines as one kind.

calendarName.description: The calendar's name when the rule was saved, shown when the provider is unreachable.

scope.description: Whose events of the type are sent: `mine` is the ones the member takes part in (for deadlines, the ones on a matter they are responsible for); `my_matters` is every one on a matter they are assigned to.

calendarName.description: The calendar's name when it was chosen, shown when the provider is unreachable.

subject.description: An event type's id, or `deadline` for deadlines as one kind.

scope.description: Whose events of the type are sent: `mine` is the ones the member takes part in (for deadlines, the ones on a matter they are responsible for); `my_matters` is every one on a matter they are assigned to.

rules.description: The member's whole rule set. A subject absent from it is not synced.

subject.description: An event type's id, or `deadline` for deadlines as one kind.

detail.description: How much of an event the firm lets leave: `full`, or `minimal` for the matter number and the event type and nothing else.

limits.description: The subjects to set. A subject not named keeps the limit it has.

calendarRemoteIds.description: The member's whole choice of calendars to be shown. A calendar absent from it is no longer read, and what was read from it is removed.

shownCalendars.description: The calendars these events are read from: the member's own choice. Empty when they have no account or chose none, in which case there is nothing to show them.

truncated.description: True when the window held more events than one answer carries.

id.description: The provider's own identifier for the event.

startsOn.description: The first day of a whole-day event, as YYYY-MM-DD. Null on a timed one.

endsOn.description: The last day a whole-day event covers. Null on a timed one.

startsAt.description: The instant a timed event starts. Null on a whole-day one. The reader's screen decides which day and hour that is.

kind.description: `changed`: the copy in the member's calendar no longer reads as it was sent. `removed`: the copy is no longer in the member's calendar. `not_sent`: the provider would not take the event, so there is no copy.

startsAtTime.description: The wall-clock start as HH:MM, or null when the copy takes the whole day.

endsOn.description: The last day the copy covers, as YYYY-MM-DD.

timeZone.description: The zone the event was recorded in. Both sides of a difference are read in it.

sent.description: The event as it was sent to the member's calendar, at the detail the firm allows.

startsAtTime.description: The wall-clock start as HH:MM, or null when the copy takes the whole day.

endsOn.description: The last day the copy covers, as YYYY-MM-DD.

timeZone.description: The zone the event was recorded in. Both sides of a difference are read in it.

found.description: The copy as the member's calendar holds it now. Null when the copy is gone.

system.description: The outside system, in whatever the addon calls itself — never an enum here, because adding one is the point. Matched case-insensitively: 'ClickUp' and 'clickup' are one system.

externalId.description: The remote's own handle for the object. Opaque: this platform never parses it, never orders by it, and never assumes a shape.

remoteRevision.description: What the remote looked like when the two sides last agreed — a vendor revision token, an ETag, a timestamp they minted. Stored and handed back, never compared for order.

callerIdentity.description: A caller ID the firm already paid for, or null when it has none for the number.

paidLookup.description: Whether a caller-ID lookup may be asked for. `unavailable` means none is provisioned; `not-covered` means no caller-name data exists for numbers in this country.

displayName.description: Null when the record holds no name at all; a reader shows the gap.

region.description: Where the area code was issued — a state, a province or a city. Where the number was issued, never where the caller is.

place.description: The town the number's exchange was assigned to, as the numbering data writes it ("Las Vegas, NV"). Null where that data does not subdivide the area code.

timeZone.description: The IANA time zone the number was issued under. Null where the area code spans several.

callerName.description: The name the carriers' caller-name database holds, as it holds it. Null when it holds none.

CallerIdentity.description: A caller ID the firm already paid for.

number.description: The number in E.164 — a plus, the country calling code and the national number, digits only. The form builds it from the number field and its country.

CallerIdentityLookup.description: `found` is the kept answer, which may hold no name. `not-covered` and `unavailable` are answers, not failures: nothing was asked and nothing was charged.

authorityBasis.description: The authority this release is made on, in the firm's own words. There is no list of acceptable answers: what suffices to release an original varies by jurisdiction.

identityEvidence.description: How the person collecting was identified. Record the check that was made, not the document's numbers — this lands on a ledger row that can never be edited or deleted.

witnessedByUserId.description: The second signatory, when the firm requires two. Must be an ACTIVE member of this firm other than the caller — the caller is recorded as the member who checked identity, so a release cannot be signed twice by one person.

description.description: What was physically found, in the observer's words. Required on an unregistered observation: it is the only record of that object anywhere.

truncated.description: TRUE when this register is larger than the reconciliation reads in one pass. A truncated report is a PARTIAL answer: packets past the cut were never expected, so they were never reported missing, and every count here is a floor rather than a finding. A count in this state cannot be closed with its numbers frozen; narrow its scope or abandon it.

TRUE when the walk was larger than the reconciliation reads in one pass. Only ever true on an abandoned close: a close that freezes counts refuses a truncated reconciliation rather than freezing a partial answer.

abandoned.description: Ends a count that was never finished. An abandoned count freezes no findings: the reconciliation of a half-done walk reads as a safe full of missing originals, which would be alarming and wrong.

question.description: What was asked, phrased as a question.

answer.description: The verified answer, phrased to stand alone with no other field beside it.

semantic.description: The meaning the machine reads, where the tag has one. Production membership, privilege logging and completion arithmetic resolve through this and never through the name, so a firm may rename a tag freely without changing what anything does. A tag a firm created carries none and drives no machinery — it filters, groups and exports.

requiredForCompletion.description: Whether a document with no answer here counts as uncoded. That arithmetic is the progress figure, so turning it on for a question most documents will not answer makes the figure mean something else.

colorToken.description: The NAME of a design token, never a colour value — the coding panel styles through the design system, and a raw value would be an off-token colour no theme could correct.

criteria.description: The filter this selection came from, as a note for whoever reads the history. Field names and identifiers only — it is never re-run, and free text here would put content into a record that has no way to redact it.

transcriptScope.description: Whether the firm's assistant transcripts are in scope for this load. Required, with no default in either direction: a transcript is the firm's own work product, and a silent exclusion decides as much for somebody as a silent inclusion would. Recorded on the load, so the manifest states what the corpus was drawn from and not only what landed in it.

taskId.description: The task this time was worked on. Must be a task on this same matter: a task on another matter, or on no matter at all, is refused. One task per entry — time that served two tasks is recorded as two entries.

memo.description: The firm's own note about the entry. Internal only: it never appears on a bill, a print sheet, or the client portal, and the audit trail records that it changed, never what it says.

incrementMinutes.description: The minimum billing increment a captured duration is rounded TO, in minutes. Six — a tenth of an hour — is the prevailing default. This is also what one BILLING UNIT is worth, which is why a screen that lets time be entered in units has to ask: a firm on quarter hours and a firm on tenths mean different amounts of work by 'two units'.

roundingDirection.description: How a duration that falls between increments is resolved.

taskId.description: The task this time was worked on. Null unlinks it; absent leaves it unchanged. A task named here must be on the entry's own matter.

memo.description: The firm-internal note. Null clears it; absent leaves it unchanged.

overrideRateE4.description: A rate for THIS entry, in ten-thousandths of a currency unit, sitting above every stored tier of the rate chain. Capture has always accepted one and the chain has always ranked it first; this is the same field on a draft the firm already holds, so an entry captured at the wrong rate is corrected rather than voided and typed again. A number sets it, null clears it and the entry falls back to the chain (matter, then client, then timekeeper, then role, then the card default) as of its work date, and absent leaves the rate exactly as it stands. Setting it re-computes the entry's amount. This does not weaken the rate snapshot: that rule says a rate card edited LATER never re-rates a standing entry, and it still holds — what changes here is somebody's deliberate answer for one entry, not a card's answer for all of them. An entry with no rate card resolves to no rate whatever is passed: an override is a rate ON a card.

get.description: Lists the firm's directory — every person and organization it holds, in name order and cursor-paged, with `total` giving the size of the whole record. People and organizations are ONE sequence: the directory is one book, and `kind` narrows it rather than splitting it. Deleted records and records folded into another by a merge are excluded — a folded record still answers a search and still resolves to its survivor, but listing it beside that survivor would show one client as two. Given `search`, the same read answers a NAME instead: the firm's ranked trigram search chooses the records and they come back as the same listing rows, in the firm's own relevance order. That answer is capped rather than walkable, so `nextCursor` is null, `total` is the size of the answer, and `capped` says whether the firm holds more matches than fitted.

put.description: Sets the firm's conflicts floor. It writes on conflicts:configure rather than conflicts:run, which is a narrower key seeded to Owner and Admin alone — this does not act on a check, it decides what every LATER check searches, and no single check row records that a person chose that. The stored value is normalized first and the normalized value is returned, so what a firm is shown is what its checks will actually run: a floor with every source deselected comes back carrying `party`. Changing the floor writes no check and re-runs nothing — a matter whose last check no longer covers the new floor reports the shortfall on its own posture read, computed live, which is why raising the floor takes effect everywhere at once with no sweep.

This read is what makes that history producible. Each entry names the reviewer, carries the rationale they gave, and for a waiver carries the waiver's own record and what that record is short of, so an answer the firm cannot evidence never reads the same as one it can. Every call appends a new row; a reviewer who reverses an earlier call records a second disposition rather than editing the first, so the full history of the adjudication stays visible. A waiver carries a record of its own: who consented, whether that consent was confirmed in writing, the filed document evidencing the confirmation, and the date the waiver was given. The consenting party and the date are required, because they are the act being recorded. A poller following a live meeting continues from `nextCursor`, which every page with rows carries whether or not more are waiting; here it is a position in the conversation rather than a has-more flag, so a reader resumes exactly where it stopped and a caller walking to the end sees one final empty page. Never continue from a timestamp alone: two messages can share an instant, and the second is lost to a reader that asks for what came strictly after it. `since` with `sinceId` is the same position spelled out for a caller that holds the pair rather than the cursor. A message that has been taken back is still returned, with an empty body beside the instant and the member that say it was removed. A caller that sends `since` also receives `redacted`: the messages taken back since that instant, which a forward walk cannot reach because a redaction moves no row's position in the ordering. Blank the body of each one you are holding; a repeat is harmless.

It carries no session description, no display name and no track name, and it changes nothing. Each participant is named by the stay and by the member handle behind it: the stay is what every frame, every event and the member's own screen correlate by, and the member handle is what joins a report of "my tile went black" — which arrives as a person, and often as the second of that person's two stays — to the room that was serving them. get.description: Lists time entries three ways. By timekeeper and work date: the daily view, complete in one page by construction, so its cursor is always null. By matter alone: the matter's own record, CURSOR-PAGED newest work date first — a matter that has been billing for years is not a single response, and this read carried no bound at all until it was. Otherwise the period listing across every matter, cursor-paged the same way: bounded by `from` and `to` (each on its own or together; neither is the whole record), narrowable to one timekeeper, one matter and one status. A period listing that names no timekeeper covers the whole firm and requires the time:viewFirm capability; one that names somebody other than the session member requires it too.

This is the firm's Time screen's Date column filter, honoured here so it is true across every page rather than over the page in hand. Without a timekeeper the listing covers everybody, which requires the time:viewFirm capability.

post.description: Returns a voided time entry to draft, with its number, its narrative, its memo, its codes, its attachments and its history intact. Voiding is how a mistaken entry is retired and it is reversible for exactly one reason: people void the wrong row, and re-typing the entry loses everything the row carries. It restores the entry to DRAFT and never to submitted or approved — those were somebody's judgement about an entry that has since been withdrawn, and they have to be given again. Refused for an entry that is not void, and for the one void that must stay one: an entry voided by conversion into a cost, where the value already moved to the cost record and restoring the time would charge the same work twice.

post.description: Moves a misfiled DRAFT entry onto another matter. Its own route rather than a PATCH of matterId, because it is a cross-matter write: two ledgers change, and the rate the entry froze was resolved against the matter it is leaving. The entry number, the description, the memo, the codes, the attachments and the whole history carry across untouched; the RATE and the ROUNDING INCREMENT are re-resolved against the destination as of the entry's own work date, because both are matter-scoped and carrying one client's answer to another is how a firm bills at the wrong rate. Refused for anything past draft, anything on a bill, and anything a draft invoice has claimed — past that the entry is evidence somebody is relying on, and the answer is a void and a fresh record.

post.description: Proposes a payment of client money out of a matter's trust ledger, and — when the firm's posture lets this member release it alone — makes the payment in the same atomic write. The firm decides which: a member holding the authority to act on client money releases an amount that needs no second person by themselves, and the response says `approved` with the movement it posted; anybody else leaves a pending request that somebody who holds the authority has to approve, and the response says `pending`, names who can approve it, and moves no money at all — no ledger entry, no balance change, no movement record. Either way the proposal is checked against the ledger's AVAILABLE balance (the stored balance less any disputed-funds holds), and a request that stays pending is checked again when it is approved.

post.description: Opens a trust account and binds it to one of the firm's offices. The jurisdiction is the office's own and is never chosen here, because the rules require a trust account to sit in the state of the lawyer's office — naming it separately would be a second answer to a question the office already settles. An office that has no jurisdiction recorded still opens an account, and every movement on that account is refused until the office records one, so recording the office's state is what makes the account usable rather than something to redo here. Only the last four digits of the bank account number are taken, because that is all the platform stores of it. The account is pooled interest-bearing unless the firm says otherwise. A retried open returns the account the first call opened rather than opening a second one, which is why the idempotency key is required.

Rows are scoped to the calling member and filtered by matter visibility at read time rather than when they were written, so a change in what a matter's notifications may show takes effect on the next read without any row being altered; today that filter excludes the platform's own internal holding matters, and any further restriction composes into the same read when it exists. A notification carries identifiers, closed labels, counts and dates only — never a title, a name, a filename or a subject line; follow the link to resolve the record it points at through that subsystem's own access-checked read. readThroughCursor names the newest row on this page and is what read-all takes as its bound; it is null only when the page is empty. Searching has an unusual shape here, and it follows from the row carrying no sentence: the words a member reads are composed by the client from the kind and the declared facts, so the client resolves a query into the `kinds` and `searchCategories` whose words match it and sends those alongside `search`, which is matched against the matter number — the one piece of member-facing text the row itself carries. The three are OR-ed; supplying none of them narrows nothing, and an empty `kinds` means the query matched no kind rather than matching no row.
